title: 'PM Asked Everyone Not to Go Abroad' — How Vijay Deverakonda Turned a Congratulations Tweet Into South Cinema's Funniest Tourism Ad
excerpt: Suriya's Karuppu crosses ₹140 crore worldwide, but it's his co-star's cheeky holiday advice — referencing Modi's domestic tourism push — that NRI Twitter can't stop sharing
body:
It started as a congratulations tweet. It ended as the most-shared tourism recommendation South Indian cinema has produced this year.

Vijay Deverakonda logged onto X on Saturday to celebrate the runaway success of Suriya's *Karuppu*, the RJ Balaji-directed fantasy action-drama that has now crossed ₹140 crore worldwide in just four days. His message was warm, generous, and exactly the kind of public camaraderie that Telugu and Tamil film industries do better than anyone: "So happy to see the overwhelming love for Karuppu in Telugu. Love love love the news, for the brilliance he has been showing us on screen, giving his everything every year... finally when the theaters are loud and noisy it fills all of us with Joy. Big congratulations Anna, please take a nice holiday..."

Suriya responded with characteristic warmth — and then dropped the question that set the internet on fire: "Haha! ఇదంతా మన ప్రియమయిన ఫ్యాన్స్ కోసం… (All this for our beloved fans!)" he wrote. "Btw which is a good holiday spot?"

## The Punchline That Became the Point

Vijay's reply arrived fast — and it was perfect: "Prime Minister asked everyone not to go abroad. So sending my Indian recommendations, where you can have some peaceful private time... on WhatsApp anna."

The tweet went massively viral, racking up millions of impressions within hours. Fans loved the warmth between two stars from different industries. Film journalists quoted it. Meme accounts remixed it. But it was the NRI corner of Twitter that truly ran with it — because for anyone in the diaspora, the joke landed on multiple levels.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has, over the past two years, repeatedly urged citizens to explore domestic destinations before booking international flights. His pitch — tied to initiatives like 'Dekho Apna Desh' and the broader push to grow India's $75 billion domestic tourism market — has resonated unevenly. Many NRIs, already planning their annual India trip around family weddings and festival seasons, found the idea both amusing and relatable.

## Karuppu's Extraordinary Weekend

The exchange arrived against the backdrop of *Karuppu*'s extraordinary box office run. Directed by RJ Balaji — who co-stars alongside Suriya and Trisha Krishnan — the film earned ₹15.50 crore on its opening day in India, surged to ₹78.8 crore domestically by Day 3, and crossed ₹120.75 crore worldwide in its first weekend.

By Day 4, worldwide collections touched ₹140 crore, with trade analysts projecting a ₹200 crore lifetime if weekday holds remain stable. The overseas performance has been particularly notable — ₹42 crore from international markets in the first weekend alone, driven heavily by the Gulf, North America, and the UK.

For Suriya, it represents a genuine career resurgence. His 45th lead role, *Karuppu* had faced production delays and financial complications, making the massive opening all the more dramatic. Reviews have praised Suriya's dual performance while noting the film's uneven second half — a pattern, ironically, that rarely hurts box office in the first week.

## Why This Moment Matters for the Diaspora

The Vijay-Suriya exchange is small, throwaway, the kind of thing that scrolls past in a feed. But it captures something NRIs recognise instantly: the changing texture of South Indian cinema's public culture.

A decade ago, cross-industry praise between Telugu and Tamil stars was rarer, and when it happened, it felt formal — press conference quotes, award show courtesies. Today, it's happening in real time on X, in Telugu and Tamil script, with inside jokes that fans decode and amplify. The diaspora, plugged into both industries simultaneously in a way that domestic audiences rarely are, gets to experience the full spectrum.

Vijay Deverakonda himself embodies this shift. His next film, *Ranabaali* — for which he recently shared footage of intense horse-riding training — is positioning itself as a pan-Indian action drama. Suriya's *Karuppu*, distributed in both Tamil and Telugu, is earning a significant share of its box office from Hindi-belt multiplexes. The walls between India's film industries are dissolving, and it's happening fastest in diaspora living rooms, where a single OTT subscription surfaces content from all four industries.

So when Vijay told Suriya to holiday in India — jokingly, warmly, with a wink at the Prime Minister — he was speaking directly to an audience that already does exactly that: plans trips home around film releases, books IMAX tickets in Edison and Sunnyvale for Telugu premieres, and follows both stars with equal devotion.

The best tourism campaigns aren't government slogans. Sometimes they're just two friends being funny on Twitter.
